intro: Lesson 68: Angles in quadrilaterals. To understand why the angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360° and use the properties of special quadrilaterals

questions.q: A quadrilateral has angles 95°, 2x, 3x and 115°. Find x.
A rhombus has an angle of 38°. Find the other three.
Can a quadrilateral have four angles of 100°?

Find the missing angles, with reasons: (a) 72°, 108°, 95° and a (b) a parallelogram with one angle 128° (c) a kite with equal angles b, b and others 64° and 100° (d) a trapezium with base angles 55° and 70°: the other two
questions.model: (a) 72 + 108 + 95 = 275; a = 360 - 275 = 85° (angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°). (d) Each slanted side: 180 - 55 = 125° and 180 - 70 = 110°.

questions.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 3 : 4. Find them and name a possible shape.
Use triangles to explain why the angles of a pentagon add up to 540°.
questions.a: Diagonals from one vertex make 3 triangles: 3 × 180° = 540°.

A parallelogram has an angle of 70°. Its neighbour?
Big question: why do the angles in every quadrilateral add up to 360°?
questions.a: A diagonal splits it into two triangles, each with 180°.
